I think about this year the same way I think every year. Last year's wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, and my maize was a bit over 500 kg per mu. Not bad. I will do mostly the same things. Changing too much is risky — my family eats from this land.

My 2.6 mu is not big. We are 7 people in the house, but some of the young ones work in the city and send money back. So the land mostly feeds us and gives a little cash. I cannot waste money, but I also cannot lose the harvest. If I skimp on fertilizer and the wheat comes out thin, that is a bigger loss than the few yuan I save.

**For the winter wheat:**
I will buy improved seed from the agricultural store in town — the same kind my neighbor Wang uses, because her field did well last autumn. I plant in early October after I clear the maize stalks. I use the rotary tiller — the man with the machine comes around and does the whole village, costs about 50 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg each bag) across my 2.6 mu as the base — that is roughly 2 bags per mu or close to it. Then at jointing time in spring, I spread urea, about half a bag per mu (25 kg). That is what everyone around here does. Going less scares me.

Water: I irrigate 3 times — once before the ground freezes so the roots survive winter, once at jointing when the stalks are rising, and once when the grain is filling. The well is shared but I get my turn.

Pesticide: I spray 2 times — once for aphids and once for rust and powdery mildew when I see spots on the leaves.

**For the summer maize:**
After wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize seed right into the stubble — no tillage, just the seeder. Zhengdan or similar, the dealer tells me what is selling well.

I use 1 bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and one topdressing of urea at the big-trumpet stage, about half a bag per mu. Maize here grows mostly on rain in July-August, but I irrigate once if it stays dry at tasseling. I spray once for corn borer.

I hope wheat gives me 450 kg per mu and maize 520 kg per mu. That is what my land usually does.
